title: A tanker hit the docked river cruise ship American Heritage in New Orleans and it capsized
dek: About 129 people were reported aboard a riverboat on the Mississippi when the collision happened. Rescues were under way and the toll was not yet known.
what: At about 12:30 p.m. Central on Friday, 13 November 2026, the tanker Atlantic Asphalt struck the river cruise ship American Heritage on the Mississippi River near the Port of New Orleans. ABC News and CBS News report that the cruise ship, operated by American Cruise Lines, was docked at the time. ABC says it had been docked for about two hours and was hit broadside. Both say it capsized and was largely submerged.

Reports put about 129 passengers, plus crew, on board, though CBS says some people had already left the ship. CBS says nearby boats pulled more than a dozen people from the water. The New Orleans Fire Department, the New Orleans Police Department and the U.S. Coast Guard are responding. ABC reports the river is closed to vessel traffic between mile markers 93 and 96.

American Cruise Lines said it is in close coordination with the Coast Guard and local authorities, and that "Guests and crew were evacuated". Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry said he was heading to New Orleans. When ABC and CBS wrote, the numbers of injured, dead and missing had not been confirmed, and officials called it an active and evolving incident.

The cause is not known. Early posts called the tanker a "cargo ship" and asked where it was going. The reports I found give no cause and no account of the tanker's movements, so those questions are unanswered here. Posts also circulated video of the capsizing. I did not use any of it as evidence for the cause.
why: A large, fast-moving rescue on a major river with video from the scene. Early posts called the vessel a cargo ship, and the first news reports corrected that to a tanker.
next: Official counts of people rescued, injured and missing. The Coast Guard and federal investigators have not said what caused the collision.
